tagline: Through the Virginia coalfields, starting inside a mine.
intro: The trail begins at the exhibition mine in Pocahontas, the first company mining town in Virginia, and runs 325 miles through seven coalfield counties in three loops. The first goes 157 miles to St. Paul by way of Tazewell, Buchanan, Dickenson, Russell and Wise counties, past more than 50 coal-related sites visible from the byway.

The Norton, Wise and Lee loop turns onto back roads through Appalachia, Pennington Gap and Big Stone Gap, past old and new mining camps. The roads there are curvy and twisty, with a few hairpin turns.

moments.title: Pocahontas Exhibition Mine
moments.text: The mine that opened the Pocahontas coalfield in 1882 became the country's first exhibition mine in 1938, and until 1970 visitors could drive their cars straight through it.

moments.title: Grundy
moments.text: After nine major floods of the Levisa Fork since 1929, the mountain across the river was blasted into level ground and much of the town moved up onto it.

moments.title: Big Stone Gap
moments.text: When coal and iron were being developed here in the 1880s, the town hoped to become the Pittsburgh of the South, a nickname the much larger Birmingham, Alabama, later took instead.
